title: TrackMem: Tracking Evolving Beliefs in Long-Horizon Financial Dialogue
abstract: arXiv:2611.02001v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memory systems for LLM agents are evaluated mostly on social dialogue, where facts accumulate and rarely change, so remembering reduces largely to finding the turn in which something was said. Financial dialogue breaks this assumption: figures are revised, stances shift without being restated, rules stated once govern later questions, and a single company is discussed under several analytical lenses. Memory systems that retrieve the passages most similar to a question, or the most recent ones, therefore return superseded values, miss rules that share no wording with the question, and cannot recover a stance spread across sessions. We present TrackMem, a per-speaker graph memory that tracks the history of figures, separates perspectives by entity and lens, and preserves each speaker's actions in chronological order. translated_title: TrackMem：追踪长程金融对话中不断演变的信念
translated_abstract: LLM智能体的记忆系统主要在社交对话上进行评估，而社交对话中事实只累积、很少改变，因此“记忆”在很大程度上就简化为找到某句话是在哪一轮说出的。金融对话打破了这一假设：数字会被修订，立场会在没有重述的情况下悄然转变，一次陈述的规则会支配后续的多个问题，同一家公司还会在多个分析视角下被反复讨论。因此，那些检索与问题最相似或最新文本片段的记忆系统，会返回已被取代的旧数值，错过与问题措辞完全不同的规则，也无法还原散布在多个会话中的立场变化。我们提出TrackMem，一种按说话者组织的图结构记忆系统，它追踪每个数字的历史演变，按实体与分析视角分离不同观点，并按时间顺序保留每个说话者的动作轨迹。为了评估该系统，我们构建了FinLoCoMo基准，包含15段长程投资对话和765个问题，涵盖两种场景设置（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出TrackMem——一种按说话者组织的图结构记忆系统，能够追踪金融对话中被修订的数字、跨会话演变的立场以及一次陈述即约束后续问题的规则，并配套发布FinLoCoMo长程投资对话基准来检验动态信念追踪能力。
en_tdlr: We present TrackMem, a per-speaker graph memory that tracks revised figures, evolving stances across sessions, and once-stated rules in long-horizon financial dialogue, together with FinLoCoMo, a benchmark of long investment conversations for evaluating dynamic belief tracking in LLM agent memory.
